correctness.rationale: Using the exact Gibbons–Veselov gamma=a band-edge factorization, w0=delta0 and wn=delta_n-delta_(n-1), where delta_n is the Dirichlet harmonic-oscillator energy excess above 2n, once delta_n>delta_(n-1) for sufficiently large a. For u_n=H_n exp(-x^2/2), differentiate the boundary-value solution with respect to energy; the Wronskian equals minus the half-line L2 mass I_n=2^(n-1)n!sqrt(pi). The growing solution u_n J_n, J_n=integral u_n^-2, gives delta_n=1/(I_n J_n(a)) up to exponentially smaller errors. Endpoint Laplace plus Hermite leading coefficients yields J_n=e^(a^2)/(2^(2n+1)a^(2n+1)) [1+(n^2+n+1)/(2a^2)+O_n(a^-4)]. Adjacent displacement ratio is n/(2a^2)+O_n(a^-4), so the relative bandwidth correction becomes (n+1)^2/2; the n=0 convention works. Independent high-precision Kummer zero calculations at n<=3, a=6,8 gave correctly signed/better two-term approximations, not an infinite proof.
